derivation.whyItLooksCorrect: That union has equalled this population on the corpora this service has run, which is a fact about those corpora and not about the two routes. It holds only while several states are unoccupied, and nothing anywhere fails when one of them stops being empty.
derivation.whyItIsWrong: The sets differ by construction, not by accident. A released payment is in this population by definition — the mandate let it through — and appears in NEITHER route: its disposition is on record so reconciliation excludes it, and no human decided it so resolutions excludes it. In the other direction reconciliation also collects `approved-unsettled` and `reported-diverged` rows, so the union is not the instructed set either. Under any corpus holding a release or an approval the two answers part company.
derivation.soWhat: A derivation that is correct on one corpus is the defect this route was built to remove. Read `reserved` from here. This route asserts the partition rather than leaving a consumer to rediscover it, and a consumer that unions two other routes has silently opted out of that assertion.

note: Every payment this mandate let through, one row each, carrying the single state it ended in. The states are exhaustive and disjoint over this population and that is asserted by this route rather than left to a consumer to rediscover by unioning two other routes. A refusal is absent by definition: it draws no budget and creates no reservation.
